newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares rose to a new record close on Monday, but without Friday's convincing momentum and largely led by Royal Dutch shares which jumped two percent after announcing merger talks of its U.S. refining operations.
The AEX index rose 2.53 points to 587.46, losing much of Wall Street inspired opening gains which pushed it to an intra-day record of 588.89.
Over one full point of the AEX advance was caused by Royal Dutch shares, which rose 5.90 guilders to 278.90. The company said it was in merger talks with Texaco and Saudi Aramco.
The underlying consolidation was expected by most dealers.
"Today was a bit slow in volume terms, but the undertone remains very good. It really shows in the reaction to the Royal Dutch news," one dealer said.

Earlier in the day another dealer said he expected the index to steam through to 600 points any day, a view supported by technical analysts which said in their weekly outlook that money flows were at record levels.

Large stocks other than Royal Dutch were mostly stable, except Unilever which benefited from gains on Wall Street where it also has a listing. But advances of shares in some medium-sized companies were all the more impressive.
The gains were ascribed to new mid-cap investment funds, ING and Insinger de Beaufort recently started such new vehicles.
Software group Cap Volmac rose 3.50 guilders, or eight percent, to 45.50. One dealer said he smelled a rat and was braced for some sort of announcement by the company.
Copier and printer maker Oce van der Grinten rose a whopping 8.30 guilders to 194.40.
Sanitary equipment maker Sphinx was the big loser, shedding 1.80 at 26.70, after abandoning merger talks with Swiss Keramik.
